title: Deeper and broader cross-kernel semantic validation and topology-identity review
mode: primary-source research and read-only local plan reconciliation
scope: Review system-agnostic CAD shape-equivalence methods and cross-CAD B-rep correspondence limits
Separate source graph and payload preservation from geometric interchangeability and topology identity
Refine the existing DWG/DXF ACIS/AcDs/kernel/native semantic gates for implementation readiness without increasing per-slice cost

method.kind: Review primary research, NIST interoperability material, current open-source route documentation, and existing local plan gates
method.limitations: Research methods and upstream documentation do not qualify a libdxfrw profile or validate a specific sample. Cross-kernel equivalence still requires a predeclared use case, independent expectations, exact payload/source provenance, and an actually executed pinned route. No external route was run.

sources.observed: The authors describe representation-independent model comparison through proxy/query methods, user-selected tolerances, and local plus global geometric/topological properties. The method is general CAD interoperability research, not DWG/DXF or ACIS conformance evidence.

The paper treats geometric and topological changes as a cross-system correspondence problem, notes that neutral exchange often lacks application-specific persistent-reference structures, and documents ambiguous/non-bijective correspondence. It does not establish preservation of any DWG/DXF object graph.

NIST describes explicit geometry and face-edge-vertex topology as distinct but related aspects of boundary representation, including hybrid model cases. This informs evidence decomposition but is not an ACIS reader or DWG mapping.

sources.project: Existing open-source ACIS and application route inventory
sources.revision: Mutable public docs reviewed 2026-10-18; detailed lineage findings remain recorded in the 2026-10-17 local plan/receipt
sources.observed: OpenCADStudio documents a kernel route with a per-surface fallback; opencadkernel self-identifies as early; cq-acis documents bounded geometry conversion limits through an OCCT-family route. These are route-specific observations, not complete-solid evidence or an independent kernel/native qualification. This pass identified no new qualified open-source route joining outer DWG/DXF/AcDs parsing to an independent kernel and native acceptance.

assessment.planImpact: Refines PAR-07/S8 so file graph and carrier identity, complete valid B-rep semantics, geometric shape equivalence, topology identity, and native consumer acceptance are separate results. The minimal semantic case uses predeclared independent analytic expectations and tolerances; cross-kernel face/edge/vertex counts remain diagnostic unless the use case requires topology preservation. Existing fast per-slice validation and composed external cadence are unchanged.

implementationReadyChecks: Keep handle/owner/carrier/AcDs payload linkage checks independent from downstream geometric equivalence.
Before a semantic run, bind the exact source entity, carrier or AcDs payload hash, parser profile, kernel route, and independently authored expected metric manifest.
For a complete-solid pass, report body/unsupported-record disposition, valid/closed topology, fallback use, diagnostics, units/transforms, and explicit metric tolerances.
Use face/edge/vertex counts and correspondence as diagnostics unless the declared operation requires topology-preserving identity; do not use them as universal cross-kernel shape equality.
Keep parser, kernel, and native-consumer observations separate; screenshots, same-kernel round trips, and partial tessellation cannot promote semantic support.
Preserve the existing fast validation cadence; run one bounded, exact-profile peer/native comparison only at the existing composed checkpoint.
Use generated in-memory or scratch-authored controls only; do not add peer/customer DWG/DXF fixtures or dependencies.
